clue.text: A bit of work, returning to problem with grass

parts.note: an erg is a small unit of work in physics

indicators.note: returning tells us the little word that follows is read from back to front

explanation.surface: Someone taking a break from a job goes back to a lawn that has gone wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: Ergot is a fungal disease that attacks rye and other cereal grasses.

clue.text: French revolutionary in German city is put out of countenance

indicators.note: in places the revolutionary's name inside the city's name

parts.note: Ems (Bad Ems) is a spa town in Germany
Paul Barras was a leader of the French Revolution and the Directory

explanation.surface: A French radical turns up in a German town and is left mortified.
explanation.walkthrough: Paul Barras led the French Directory after Robespierre fell; Bad Ems is a spa town in Germany, so 'in' puts one name inside the other.
explanation.definitionFit: To put someone out of countenance is an old idiom for making them abashed or self-conscious.

clue.text: Physicist, American, going into fuel supply

indicators.note: going into says one piece is put inside the other

parts.note: gas is a fuel supplied to homes

explanation.surface: An American scientist gets involved in providing fuel.
explanation.definitionFit: Carl Friedrich Gauss was a German mathematician and physicist, remembered in the unit of magnetic flux density.

clue.text: This could produce a wet part

definitions.text: This could produce a wet part

indicators.note: could produce suggests the letters may be rearranged to make something new

explanation.surface: A riddle about what makes a patch damp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could produce' rearranges the letters of A WET PART; and the whole clue also describes the answer, since water from a tap leaves a wet patch.
explanation.definitionFit: Water from a household faucet is exactly the thing that would make some area damp.

clue.text: Bound to give accurate representation, pocketing minimum payment

indicators.note: pocketing means one piece holds another inside it
a representation of the word accurate presents its letters in another form

parts.note: P, a penny, is the smallest payment possible

explanation.surface: Someone is obliged to portray events faithfully while taking only a token fee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'representation' is the anagram signal, and 'pocketing' sets the penny inside the rearranged letters; 'Bound' is a leap, not tied or obliged.
explanation.definitionFit: To cut a caper is to leap or frisk about, so it means to jump.

clue.text: Taking rake-off European offered

parts.note: a cut is a share of the profits, a rake-off

explanation.surface: Someone accepts a share of the profits a European put on the table.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taking' is the adjective meaning charming or attractive, not the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Something taking is appealing or delightful, the sense of charmingly attractive.

clue.text: Capsize vessel between times? Don't start to go too fast

indicators.note: between puts the vessel in the middle of the two letters for times

parts.note: T is short for time, so times gives two of them
an urn is a vessel

indicators.note: Don't start says the word loses its opening letter

parts.note: to hurtle is to rush along at excessive speed

explanation.surface: A boat runs into trouble in the gaps between shifts, and someone is warned against speeding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'between' puts the vessel between two time abbreviations; 'Don't start' trims the first letter from the speeding verb. 'vessel' suggests a boat, matching the capsize surface, but it is a pot.
explanation.definitionFit: To turn turtle is an idiom for a boat flipping upside down.

clue.text: Risk being left out of exclusive part of church

indicators.note: being out of says the letter is taken away from the word

parts.note: the chancel is the part of a church near the altar, reserved for clergy and choir

explanation.surface: A gamble is taken by someone excluded from a private area of a church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being left out of' removes L from CHANCEL.
explanation.definitionFit: A chance is a gamble or hazard, just as a risk is.

clue.text: Seen in chamber, member with a severe hairstyle

parts.note: a po is a chamber pot
MP is a Member of Parliament
dour means stern or severe

explanation.surface: A parliamentarian with a forbidding look is noticed in the debating chamber.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chamber' looks like the Commons but is a chamber pot, PO in British slang.
explanation.definitionFit: A pompadour is a style with the hair swept up high off the forehead.

clue.text: Western show travelled round

parts.note: rode means travelled on horseback or in a vehicle
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: A cowboy display is visited by someone on a circuit.
explanation.definitionFit: A rodeo is an exhibition of cowboy skills such as bronco riding, typical of the American West.

clue.text: Tory safe, having shown readiness to go overseas

parts.note: blue is the colour of the Tories, the UK Conservatives, so a Tory is a blue
peter is old criminal slang for a safe

explanation.surface: A Conservative in a secure seat has signalled willingness to travel abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: PETER is underworld slang for a safe. The blue peter is a flag hoisted on a ship to show it is about to sail.
explanation.definitionFit: A blue peter is the signal flag a ship flies when it is ready to put to sea.

clue.text: Injured, not originally carrying a weapon

indicators.note: not originally says the opening letter is dropped

parts.note: harmed means injured

explanation.surface: A hurt person was not, at first, holding a gun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not originally' drops the first letter, H, from HARMED.
explanation.definitionFit: Being armed means having a gun or other weapon with you.

clue.text: Car's wrecked by a person unqualified to drive, a rogue

indicators.note: wrecked suggests the word is smashed up and put back together differently

parts.note: L stands for learner, a driver not yet qualified

explanation.surface: A car is written off by a learner driver, a real villain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrecked' rearranges CARS into RASC; L is the learner plate.
explanation.definitionFit: A rascal is a scoundrel or mischievous villain.

clue.text: Musical rejected by censor giving instruction to musicians

indicators.note: rejected means the show's title is turned back on itself

parts.note: Cats is the Lloyd Webber musical
Cato the Elder held the Roman office of censor

explanation.surface: A stage show is turned down by an official censor who then advises the band.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' turns the musical's title round; Cato the Elder was famous as the stern Roman censor.
explanation.definitionFit: Staccato is a marking telling players to make notes short and detached.

clue.text: Home bird provided homely dish

parts.note: a cottage is a small home
pie is an old name for the magpie

explanation.surface: A domestic bird made a simple supper.
explanation.walkthrough: PIE for magpie is an old crossword standby.
explanation.definitionFit: Cottage pie is a plain British dish of minced beef topped with mashed potato.

clue.text: Sailor, having fallen off boat, runs away openly

parts.note: AB, able-bodied seaman, is a sailor

indicators.note: away says the letter goes missing from the word

parts.note: overboard means having fallen from a ship into the water
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A seaman tumbles over the side and the crew make off in plain sight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'runs away' removes R (runs, a cricket abbreviation) from OVERBOARD, leaving OVEBOARD.
explanation.definitionFit: Above board means honestly and without concealment.

clue.text: In difficulty immediately

definitions.meaning: in an awkward position, under pressure
at once, right then and there

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means both put in an awkward position and doing something then and there.

clue.text: Person in charge of stud

definitions.meaning: a raised knob or ornamental stud on a surface

explanation.definitionFit: A boss is both a manager and a raised ornamental knob like a stud.

clue.text: Illumination? A lot needed round food store

indicators.note: round says one piece goes about the other

parts.note: a sight is colloquial for a great deal, as in a sight better
a deli is a delicatessen, a food shop

explanation.surface: A big lamp is wanted to light up a grocery.
explanation.walkthrough: SIGHT meaning a lot, as in 'a sight too much', is the colloquialism to spot.
explanation.definitionFit: A sidelight is a small lamp on a vehicle, a source of light.

clue.text: Inconvenient drawn out readjusted

indicators.note: readjusted means the letters are set in a new order

explanation.surface: A tediously long matter has been altered again.
explanation.definitionFit: Untoward means unfavourable or awkward, causing trouble.

clue.text: One of the first men seeing alien keeping quiet about it?

indicators.note: keeping means one piece holds the other inside

parts.note: sh is the call for quiet
ET is the film's extraterrestrial

explanation.surface: An early human sees a spaceman and is told to stay silent about it.
explanation.walkthrough: Seth was the third son of Adam and Eve.
explanation.definitionFit: Seth, son of Adam, belongs to the earliest generation of humans in Genesis.

clue.text: Rushes around carrying a fish, where food was short during siege

definitions.text: where food was short during siege

indicators.note: carrying means the outer piece holds the others inside
around says the word is turned the other way

parts.note: darts means rushes
ling is a sea fish

explanation.surface: Someone hurries about with a fish, in a city starved under blockade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' turns the rushes backwards and 'carrying' puts A and the fish inside. The siege of Stalingrad in 1942-43 brought famine to the city.
explanation.definitionFit: The Soviet city was besieged in 1942-43 and its people endured famine.

clue.text: Puts up with soldiers being lethargic

indicators.note: up in a down clue says the word is read bottom to top

parts.note: OR is other ranks, ordinary soldiers

explanation.surface: Someone tolerates the troops while feeling sluggish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses PUTS to STUP in this down entry; OR is other ranks.
explanation.definitionFit: A stupor is a dazed state, a condition of torpor and lethargy.

clue.text: Standing up, rest I get's restricted

indicators.note: restricted says the letters are held within the run of words

explanation.surface: A person on their feet finds their break is cut short.
explanation.walkthrough: The print drops the I; the hidden letters run up, rest I get's.
explanation.definitionFit: Standing as a noun means status or reputation.

clue.text: Don, still in bed, gets up

indicators.note: gets up in a down clue says the phrase is read upwards

parts.note: not up means still in bed

explanation.surface: A university lecturer is having a lie-in, then rises.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Don' is the verb, to dress in, not the academic. 'gets up' reverses NOT UP.
explanation.definitionFit: To don clothes is to dress in them.

clue.text: Magistrate has no time to seek advice

indicators.note: has no says the letter is removed

parts.note: to consult is to seek advice

explanation.surface: A busy official cannot find a moment to ask for guidance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has no time' removes T from CONSULT.
explanation.definitionFit: In ancient Rome a consul was one of the two chief magistrates.

clue.text: End with nothing inside a dive

indicators.note: inside places one piece within the other

parts.note: to stop is to end
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A sordid bar finally closes with nobody in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dive' looks like a seedy bar, but is the plunge of a hawk on its prey.
explanation.definitionFit: A stoop is the swift downward swoop of a bird of prey.

clue.text: A thousand some regarded as a large number

parts.note: M is the Roman numeral for a thousand
any can mean some, as in have you any

explanation.surface: A thousand people are considered by some to be quite a crowd.
explanation.definitionFit: Many means numerous, a great quantity.

clue.text: Give a refill to whelp

parts.note: to whelp is to give birth ..., ...

explanation.surface: Someone tops up a dog's bowl after she has had puppies.
explanation.definitionFit: To top up is to fill a glass or tank again.

clue.text: Cooperate for a while with dad, about to plant pine

indicators.note: about means one piece is wrapped around the other

parts.note: pa is dad
to lay is to set down or place
to long is to pine for something

explanation.surface: A child helps father put in a pine tree for a time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pine' looks like the tree but is the verb, to yearn.
explanation.definitionFit: To play along is to go along with something for the time being, going through the motions.

clue.text: Bad reputation -one I try to change

indicators.note: change signals the letters are put into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone with a poor name resolves to reform.
explanation.definitionFit: Notoriety is fame for something bad, infamy.

clue.text: In the station, drank a lot, knocking it back

indicators.note: knocking it back says the word is turned back to front

parts.note: to tope is to drink heavily

explanation.surface: A railwayman boozed at the terminus, downing pints.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knocking it back' looks like drinking but signals the reversal of TOPED.
explanation.definitionFit: A depot is a bus or railway station or garage.
